Tailwind by default. The scaffold puts <script src='/_internal/tailwind.js'> in static/partials/head.html, which every page includes; every utility class works with no build step. Style with utility classes directly in markup (className=/class=).

styles.css is ONLY for what Tailwind can't express - keyframes, @font-face, third-party widget overrides, design-token CSS variables beyond Tailwind's palette. Do NOT write component CSS (`.save-btn`). The scaffold's styles.css holds one rule (`[hidden] { display: none !important; }`, keep it) and is otherwise empty on purpose.

Extract on the SECOND use, not the third. The scaffold ships static/components/ui.tsx with canonical primitives - Button, Input, Field, Card, Badge, EmptyState. When the same class string appears in a second file, move it into the shared components module and point both at the one primitive. This is the deterministic fix for the 'every page looks slightly different by week 3' failure mode.

Dark mode is class-based: a `dark:` utility applies to elements inside an element with class `dark`, and never follows the visitor's system setting. The scaffold's pages set `class="dark"` on `<html>`, so a new app is dark (`mode: dark` in app.yaml styles the pages the server renders; pages under static/ are served as written). Remove the class from each page's `<html>` for a light app. Put `dark:` classes on `<body>` and below: one on the element that carries `dark` itself does not apply. Give every input an explicit text and placeholder colour beside its background, paired light and dark (`text-zinc-900 dark:text-zinc-100 placeholder-zinc-400 dark:placeholder-zinc-500`), as the scaffold's inputs do.
